messages.author: efb064044f1e1c0f
messages.subject: Re: Combining geom_bar and geom_smooth
parts:
So if I then instead use the reshape package to recast the data according to the facet operation I should be OK.

y1<-c(2003:2007)
y2<-as.factor(c(1:5))
y3<-as.factor(c(1:2))
y4<-as.factor(c(1:7))
y5<-c(0:90)
m<-data.frame(cbind(sample(y1,5000,replace=T),sample(y2,5000,replace=T),sample(y3,5000,replace=T),sample(y4,5000,replace=T),sample(y5,5000,replace=T)))
names(m)<-c("y1","y2","y3","y4","y5")
ggplot(m,aes(x=y1,color=y3,fill=y3,group=y3))+geom_bar(bin=1)+facet_grid(facets=y2~y4)+opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(size=10,angle=90,hjust=1))
k<-melt(m,id=c("y1","y2","y3","y4"))
k2<-cast(m,y1+y2+y3+y4~.,length)
names(k2)[5]<-"l"
x11()
ggplot(k2,aes(x=y1,y=l,color=y3,fill=y3,group=y3))+geom_line()+facet_grid(facets=y2~y4)

However the bars in the first plot and the lines in the second plot dont much up. I guess I´m off in the recasting, but I am not able to figure out what. What is wrong here?

Regards,

Moleps

messages.author: 40f327279f5af749
messages.subject: Re: Combining geom_bar and geom_smooth
parts:
> However the bars in the first plot and the lines in the second plot dont much up. I guess I´m off in the recasting,
> but I am not able to figure out what. What is wrong here?

When I run your code, they do match up. However, this is hard to see
because the bars are stacked while the lines are overplotted. If you
add position="dodge" to your bar graph this is easier to see:
ggplot(m,aes(x=y1,color=y3,fill=y3,group=y3))
+geom_bar(bin=1,position="dodge")+facet_grid(fa­
cets=y2~y4)+opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(size=10,angle=90,hjust=1))

adamk
